Show the arithmetic and assumptions

Fixed mission cost F = 100 units; variable cost V = 20 per batch. Dedicated: (F + V) / q. Shared: (F / n + V) / q, where n is occupied compatible slots and q is accepted-batch yield.

The comparison assumes identical yield, no added coordination cost and sufficient power, thermal and return capacity. It excludes financing, regulation and additional infrastructure. It is not a quote, price estimate or forecast.

Durable componentsA small membrane or reactor core performs work repeatedly.
Process knowledgeA flight can improve Earth production without recurring orbital manufacturing.
Seeds or mastersUseful only when the relevant advantage survives proven replication.

COMPLEMENTARY DATA

Connect structure to candidate selection.

CoRE MOF 2024 can support terrestrial structure and descriptor screening. Combine it with processing evidence without treating it as labeled orbital-performance data.

A USEFUL NEGATIVE CASE

Let unexpected outcomes count.

ACE-T4 studied gels after a hardware-related delay changed its samples. Such records can help identify alternative uses and prevent an “orbit always wins” model.

How to build a defensible analysis pipeline

1. Preserve provenance. Keep accession, run, sample, conditions, file keys and calibration together. Distinguish version changes from a full file manifest.

2. Measure a narrow target. Begin with interface motion, particle order or assembly timing that the imagery actually supports.

3. Hold out entire runs. Adjacent video frames are correlated. Random frame splits can make a model look far more capable than it is.

4. Link to function. Morphology is a proxy until linked to cooling, separation, optics or another measured outcome.

5. Compare the strongest Earth route. Chemistry, apparatus and processing history can confound apparent gravity effects.

6. Choose the next informative experiment. Use uncertainty to allocate scarce orbital capacity; avoid a universal “space benefit” score trained on heterogeneous studies.

THE ECOSYSTEM IS ALREADY FORMING

Build a clear role within it.

Modular platforms and orbital manufacturing are already being pursued. Our proposed differentiation is cross-material recipe development, experiment/production scheduling, bounded control and evidence-linked batch qualification.

Space Cargo Unlimited / BentoBoxModular monitored payload platform; substantial overlap with shared services.

Redwire / SpaceMDAnnounced a 2028 Starfall mission with expected capacity for up to 32 PIL-BOX systems. A plan, not a completed mission.

G-SPACEExisting PSI image analytics and space/Earth comparison tools.

Space ForgeOrbital seeds followed by terrestrial scale-up; a useful architecture already under development.

Protect the customer’s IP. Separate private formulations and batch data. Share process knowledge only where authorized.

Earn the economic claim. Count integration, hardware, power, return, failures and qualification—not only launch cost per kilogram.

Start narrowly, design broadly. One cartridge family and a matched Earth baseline are enough to test the platform thesis.

A 90-SECOND NARRATIVE

Some of the materials we need on Earth are limited by how they form. Gravity moves particles and fluids while crystals, pores and networks are taking shape.

Researchers have already used orbit to study cancer-drug formulations, pharmaceutical solid forms and ordered materials. But a successful experiment is only the beginning. Industry needs a process it can repeat.

Orbital Foundry is our proposal for that next layer: specialized manufacturing cartridges, a shared operating system and a network that connects laboratories on Earth to production capacity in space.

A lab brings a formulation and a target. We help select the experiment, schedule the process, observe its progress and connect the returned material to a complete batch record. SpaceX provides relevant routes to orbit and back; Grok can help organize the evidence and coordinate validated analytical tools.

At Cal Hacks, we make that future concrete with real NASA data and a transparent production-planning prototype. The ambition is a new industrial base above Earth—whose value is measured in better products and processes below.

Everyday impact.
